name: Kingdom of Kashmir
alt: Kashmir under the Karkota, Utpala and Lohara dynasties

predecessors.name: Alchon Huns
predecessors.text: Kashmir, where the Karkota dynasty is 'Preceded by: Alchon Huns; Gonanda dynasty (II)'

successors.name: Kashmir Sultanate
successors.text: the Kashmir Valley and its dependencies under Shah Mir: 'The Shah Miris ruled from 1339 until they were deposed by the Chak warlords and nobles in 1561'

ledger.x: 625: Durlabhavardhana founds the Karkota dynasty in Kashmir.
656: the Gilgit-Baltistan and Ladakh edge leaves the shape.

c. 661: Kashmir joins the struggle for Baltistan and Ladakh. 'From around 660 CE, the Tang dynasty and the Tibetan Empire started contesting the' Tarim Basin; 'Karkota Empire and the Umayyad Caliphate too joined the contest for Xinjiang soon afterwards'; 'Baltistan and Ladakh were at the centre of these struggles.'…

c. 724: Lalitaditya founds Parihasapura. 'established several towns, including a new capital at Parihasapura'; Srinagara 'continued to serve'. The page gives no founding year; the start of the reign (c. 724/5) is used.
732: the Himachal and Jammu hills leave Cliopatria's shape.

c. 736: Lalitaditya makes Yashovarman of Kannauj acknowledge him. 'Kalhana describes a long war and a submission. Stein accepted the victory as historical'; Jacobi dates it 14 August 733, Stein 'before 736 CE', Mishra after 736 and before Yashovarman's death in 749-753; Mishra: 'Yashovarman acknowledged his suzerainty…
747: the Tang take Little Palur.
748: Ladakh and Baltistan are Tibetan.

c. 749: Yashovarman's Kannauj is independent again. 'Yashovarman acknowledged his suzerainty briefly, then became practically independent' (Mishra); his death is placed in 749-753. 749 is the earliest of those dates.
772: the Himachal and Jammu hills return to Cliopatria's shape.
855: Avantivarman ends the Karkotas and founds the Utpala dynasty.
c. 855: the Utpalas rule from Avantipur. Infobox 'Capital: Avantipur'; the page dates no move.
860: Cliopatria widens the shape by 241 cells.
1003: the Lohara kings rule from Srinagar.
8 August 1003: Samgramaraja founds the Lohara dynasty.
1015: Mahmud of Ghazni besieges Loharkot.
1021: Mahmud's second attempt fails at Loharkot too.
1056: the Jammu side leaves Cliopatria's shape.
1152: Cliopatria widens the shape by 199 cells (Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal; Ladakh and Gilgit-Baltistan dropped).
1210: the Pothohar and Punjab foothills join Cliopatria's shape.
1320: Zulju's Mongols enter Kashmir.
1320: Zulju leaves with his plunder.
1320: the Ladakhi noble Rinchan takes the throne and becomes the first Muslim ruler.
1323: the Lohara line returns.
1338: the Shah Mir-Lohara war begins.
1339: Shah Mir takes the throne.
1339: Hindu rule in Kashmir ends and the Shah Mir sultanate begins.

wars.name: Tang-Tibetan struggle for Baltistan, Ladakh and the Tarim Basin (Karkota involvement)
wars.outcome: The Tang took Little Palur (Gilgit Valley) in 747 'after three failed attempts'; Ladakh stayed Tibet-aligned ('may have owed its primary allegiance to Tibet').

wars.name: Lalitaditya's campaigns (Yashovarman of Kannauj and the legendary conquests)
wars.outcome: Kalhana records a long war and Yashovarman's submission; the dates (733, before 736, after 736) and the reach of the other conquests (Gauda, Kalinga, Lata, Sindh, Punjab, the Tarim Basin) are disputed, Stein calling them 'manifestly legendary' and Huntington…

wars.name: Hindu Shahi expedition of Gopalavarman
wars.outcome: 'Gopalavarman led a famed expedition against a rebel Hindu Shahi king of Udabhanda c.

wars.name: Ghaznavid attempts on Kashmir (Siege of Lohkot)
wars.outcome: Mahmud of Ghazni failed twice at the fort of Loharkot (a month's siege, then 1021, blocked by snow) and 'did not attempt to invade Kashmir again'; Samgramaraja also sent an army under Tunga to help the Kabul Shahi Trilochanapala, who was defeated.

wars.name: Zulju's invasion of Kashmir
wars.outcome: The Qara'unas plundered the Valley and left; Suhadeva fled to Kishtwar and was overthrown by Rinchan, who took the throne in 1320.

wars.name: Shah Mir-Lohara War
wars.outcome: Shah Mir, a councillor of Rinchan, overthrew Kota Rani and took the throne as Shamsu'd-Din Shah in 1339.

certainty.note: Only the Kashmir Valley, ringed by mountains, has a natural boundary; every periphery (Jammu and Pir Panjal hills, Himachal, Poonch, Rajauri, Kishtwar, Gilgit) is approximate and mostly undated on the pages.
